claim.qualifier: EPA combined-cycle range, 2025 Long Range AWD

reality.qualifier: Independent 75 mph testing on 2024–2025 Long Range AWD typically yields ~300–310 mi (Recharged synthesis). Out of Spec's 70 mph test on the 'Highland' refresh achieved 370 mi — beating EPA — but their methodology runs ideal conditions. Mid-point of independent test distribution is ~305 mi at typical interstate speeds.
reality.verbatim_quote: Real‑world 70–75 mph highway range typically lands around 80–87% of the EPA number for current Model 3 variants.

sources.name: Out of Spec Studios — 'Highland' refresh 70 mph test (370 mi achieved, ideal conditions)

narrative_one_liner: Tesla Model 3 LR AWD 346 mi EPA; typical 75 mph testing 300–310 mi (~12% gap); Out of Spec ideal conditions hit 370 mi.
narrative: Tesla advertises 346 mi EPA combined for the 2025 Model 3 Long Range AWD. Recharged's synthesis of independent tests puts typical 75 mph highway range at 300–310 mi (~12–14% gap). Notably, Out of Spec's instrumented 70 mph test achieved 370 mi on the 'Highland' refresh — exceeding EPA — making this product a partial counter-example: in ideal conditions Model 3 can match or beat EPA, but typical highway driving still falls short.
methodology_notes: Two independent sources point in different directions: Recharged synthesis (typical conditions) shows shortfall; Out of Spec (ideal conditions) shows excess. We use the Recharged midpoint (305 mi) as the 'typical reality' value, with Out of Spec as a corroborating data point on the upper bound.
caveats: Out of Spec's 370-mi result is a single test at favorable conditions and does not generalize.
Highland refresh (Sep 2023+) materially improved efficiency vs. earlier Model 3 — gap depends on which generation you measure.
Compared to Model Y LR AWD's larger gap (~22%), Model 3 is closer to EPA, suggesting Tesla's sedan platform is less optimistic in its EPA filings than its SUV platform.
alternative_explanations: Software update efficiency improvements may have closed the gap further since cited tests; verify Phase 2.
Tire choice (19in standard vs 18in aero or 20in sport) shifts efficiency by 5–10%.
